hr_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me complete a compliance step in hiring an international contractor: determining the correct worker classification (contractor vs. employee) before setting up the engagement in Deel. If I haven't provided them yet, ask me for: the contractor's country and city of residence, the role/title and general job duties, expected weekly hours, contract duration (fixed-term or ongoing), whether they'll use their own equipment and set their own schedule, whether they'll work exclusively for me or serve other clients, and whether they'll direct their own work methods or follow my direct supervision.

Once you have these details, research that country's legal tests for independent contractor vs. employee status (e.g., control over work, integration into the business, financial independence, exclusivity, duration of relationship, and any local statutory tests or misclassification penalties). Summarize the applicable local test in plain language and apply it to my specific facts.

Produce a short classification memo that includes: (1) the recommended classification (contractor or employee) with reasoning tied to the facts I gave, (2) key misclassification risk factors present in this engagement, (3) any red flags suggesting the role looks more like disguised employment, and (4) recommended next steps if reclassification or additional safeguards are needed (e.g., limiting exclusivity, clarifying deliverables-based pay, using a compliant contractor agreement).

Do not draft or send any contracts yet — this step is purely to determine classification. Report back with the completed memo in plain text, clearly labeled with the recommended classification, the reasoning, and any risk flags, so I can review it before proceeding to agreement drafting in Deel.

hr_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft an international contractor agreement using {{vendor}}, our payroll/compliance platform, as part of hiring an international contractor. Before starting, ask me for any missing details: contractor's full name and country of residence, role/title, scope of work, compensation amount and currency, payment schedule (e.g., monthly, milestone-based), contract start date and duration (or 'ongoing'), and any specific clauses I want included (IP assignment, confidentiality, termination notice period, etc.).

Once you have these inputs, log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials and prepare a new contractor contract/agreement using the platform's contract creation feature, populating it with the details I provided, ensuring local compliance fields (currency, country-specific terms) are filled in correctly. Also prepare the agreement so it is ready to be sent for e-signature and stored in the contractor's records once approved.

Do NOT send the agreement to the contractor, submit it for signature, or finalize/activate the contract. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before any changes are applied, so after preparing the draft, stop for human sign-off.

When done, report back with: a summary of the contract terms you entered, a link or reference to the draft contract within {{vendor}}, any fields the platform flagged as incomplete or requiring compliance review, and a clear note confirming the draft is ready and awaiting my review and approval before it is sent.

hr_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for legal counsel's review of an international contractor agreement generated via Deel, as part of hiring an international contractor. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the contractor's name/country, (b) the location of the draft agreement (Deel dashboard link or exported file), (c) my counsel's name/email if I have one lined up, and (d) any specific compliance concerns I want flagged (e.g., IP assignment, non-compete enforceability in the contractor's jurisdiction, tax/permanent-establishment risk, termination clauses).

2. Retrieve or open the draft agreement from Deel using my configured credentials, and produce a clean summary covering: parties and scope of work, payment terms, IP/confidentiality clauses, termination provisions, governing law/jurisdiction, and any cross-border compliance clauses (worker classification, data protection, local labor law references).

3. Draft a concise cover note to counsel that includes the summary above, highlights any clauses that look unusual or high-risk based on the document text, and lists specific questions for counsel to answer (e.g., enforceability of non-compete in [country], adequacy of IP assignment language, classification risk).

4. Prepare a tracking checklist noting: date sent to counsel, expected turnaround, and a placeholder for counsel's verdict (approved / needs changes / rejected).

5. Since only a licensed attorney can judge enforceability and cross-border compliance exposure, do not evaluate legal sufficiency yourself, do not approve or bless the agreement language, and do not send the agreement on my behalf if that requires an action only I can authorize — stop for human sign-off once the summary, cover note draft, and checklist are ready.

6. Report back with: the summary, the drafted cover note, the checklist, and a note that this task now waits on counsel's asynchronous response, which I will need to check and log manually.

hr_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me send an international contractor's agreement out for e-signature using {{vendor}}, our payroll/contractor management platform, as part of hiring an international contractor. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in {{vendor}}: the contractor's full legal name, email address, the finalized contract/agreement document or template to use, and which internal approver (if any) needs to review before sending.

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Locate or create the contractor's record and attach the finalized agreement document to it.
3. Prepare the document for e-signature by filling in the contractor's name, email, role, and any other required fields in {{vendor}}'s document workflow.
4. Set up the signature routing (contractor and any internal signer) exactly as required by our standard process.
5. Save the prepared, ready-to-send document as a draft in {{vendor}} — do not click send yet.

Because approval is explicitly required from a human before changes are applied, do not actually send the document for signature yourself. Instead, prepare a summary showing: contractor name, document type, recipients in the signature order, and a link or reference to the draft in {{vendor}}. Then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: confirmation that the document is fully prepared and attached to the correct contractor record in {{vendor}}, the signature routing you set up, a link/reference to the draft, and a clear note that the send action is pending my explicit approval. Do not send, submit, or approve anything on my behalf — only prepare the draft and summary.

hr_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the payment schedule setup for a new international contractor inside {{vendor}}, as part of our contractor onboarding process. This requires final human approval before anything is committed, so you must stop short of submitting or confirming payment.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: the contractor's name/profile in {{vendor}}, the signed agreement's payment terms (amount, currency, pay frequency — weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, or monthly), the team or department they belong to, and the start date for payments.

Then, using our configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and navigate to the payment schedule setup screen for this contractor. Cross-check the signed agreement details against what you enter: pay amount, local currency, cadence, and team assignment. Pre-fill the payment schedule form in {{vendor}} exactly matching the agreement — do not alter amounts, currency, or frequency from what's specified. If {{vendor}} supports multiple schedules across teams, make sure this contractor is placed under the correct one.

Once the form is filled out and ready for review, take a screenshot or export a summary of the entered schedule (contractor name, amount, currency, frequency, team, start date) for my review. Do NOT click submit, confirm, approve, or otherwise commit the payment schedule — this step must stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: (1) confirmation the schedule was drafted and matches the agreement terms, (2) the summary of entered values, (3) any discrepancies or missing fields you found between the agreement and what {{vendor}} allowed you to enter, and (4) a clear note that the setup is awaiting my final approval before funds are committed.

hr_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me track the tax-info step for a new international contractor being onboarded through {{vendor}}. The contractor must complete their own tax residency, identification, and bank details inside {{vendor}}'s self-serve onboarding flow — this data entry can only be done by the contractor themselves and remains a human step that no agent can perform on their behalf.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for any missing details you need: the contractor's full name, email address, country of tax residency, and the {{vendor}} workspace/org name if relevant.
2. Using my configured credentials, check the {{vendor}} dashboard (or API) for this contractor's onboarding status to confirm whether the self-serve invitation has been sent, and if not, prepare a reminder or resend request for me (draft only — do not send anything without my confirmation).
3. If the invitation has already been sent, poll or check the status periodically (or tell me how to check) to see whether the contractor has completed their tax form (e.g., equivalent to W-4/I-9 for domestic hires, or the appropriate international tax form) and bank details submission.
4. Once complete, verify that the status shows the tax and banking sections as fully submitted, and note the completion date.
5. If the contractor's submission is still pending, prepare a polite reminder message draft for me to review and send myself.

Report back with: current onboarding status (pending/completed), what specific fields remain outstanding if any, the date you last checked, and any draft reminder message prepared. Do not attempt to fill in or submit any tax or banking information on the contractor's behalf — this must be done directly by the contractor in {{vendor}}. Flag clearly that this remains a human step until the contractor's submission is confirmed complete.
